items.title: Latency differences
items.claim: L1 cache access takes about 1 ns. Roughly how long does a fetch from main memory take by comparison?
items.reveal:
Approximate figures (Jeff Dean's 'numbers everyone should know'): L1 cache 1 ns, main memory 100 ns, SSD 100 microseconds, disk seek 10 ms.

The ratios drive cache-friendly algorithm design.
items.why: Algorithm choice often matters less than memory layout once data exceeds cache size.

items.title: BGP runs the internet on trust
items.claim: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) is how internet networks decide routes between each other. What is its main security weakness?

options.text: BGP is fully secured by default
Historically, BGP accepted any 'route announcement' from connected networks without cryptographic verification; misconfiguration or malice can hijack traffic globally within minutes
BGP only works inside data centres

items.reveal:
BGP was standardised in 1989 (RFC 1105). It assumes participating networks announce only routes they actually serve. Famous incidents: Pakistan Telecom's 2008 attempt to block YouTube nationally inadvertently routed YouTube traffic globally into a black hole for 2 hours; the 2021 Facebook outage was triggered by a BGP misconfiguration that withdrew Facebook's routes worldwide.

RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure) is being rolled out to cryptographically authenticate route origins, but adoption is partial.
items.why: The internet's most foundational routing protocol assumes goodwill among operators. The system works astonishingly well most of the time and fails spectacularly when it doesn't.
